pairs.why: A's long, flowing, see-through tentacles and pink bell match the real jellyfish's shape and translucency better than B's short, bunched frills.
B is a plain dark-navy can with three lenses like the real card, while A adds barn-door flaps that the real spotlight doesn't have.
A's bright yellow plastic trim makes it read as a toy, while B keeps the real card's calm, matte navy-and-grey finish.
The two are very close, but B hangs from a solid stem mount under a level truss, which is a little nearer to how the real fixture is built.
B has smoother, flatter green areas and less wrinkled paper and terrain detail, so it is nearer the real card's clean, simple map.
B's thick white rim and flat bright-green sheets match the real card's main colours, while A reads as cream, crumpled paper; B is a bit glossier than the real card, though.
B's lighter rim and cleaner, less crumpled sheets are slightly closer to the real card's white-bordered map than A's beige paper.
B's thin metal pole, scalloped red, yellow and orange panels and tilted angle match the real umbrella, while A is a puffy, balloon-like canopy on a thick, toy-like pole.
